comment: Planet presets (stages 1b and 1c-A). axialTilt: degrees between the spin axis and the orbit (0-180; Earth 23.4, Uranus 97.8: it lies on its side, so each pole has decades of day and then of night). eccentricityPerMille: how stretched the orbit is (Earth 17, Mars 93); the planet is closest to its star at the northern winter solstice. Star and orbit (real formulas, decision of 2026-11-05): give exactly two of luminosity (star brightness in Suns), distance (astronomical units, Earth 1), yearLength (Earth years) and light (sunlight compared with Earth); the rest follows: light = luminosity / distance^2, star mass from its brightness (main sequence), year from Kepler's third law. Every planet must lie in the habitable zone: light from 0.356 to 1.107 of Earth's. Air: otherGases is the pressure of nitrogen and oxygen in bar (Earth 1); co2 in bar is optional: when missing it comes from the carbon cycle, where volcanoes (volcanism, percent of Earth's) add CO2 and weathering on warm, ice-free land takes it out again. The CO2 gives the greenhouse warming (Earth: 280 ppm, 33 C) and adds to the pressure; thick air softens the seasons. water, moisture, relief: the land of the preset; any value can be changed after choosing a preset. seasons: when one step of stepsPerYear lasts at least minStepMonths (a year of 8 Earth years or more), a turn is one step of the planet's year (unless the era's turn is shorter) and the seasons are played turn by turn: nothing grows in winter, hunting still gives winterFoodPercent of the wild food. Shorter years are averaged into the climate. Mars is a Mars-like planet at Mars's distance from a Sun: far more volcanic than Earth (like a young Tharsis), so its thick CO2 air keeps it habitable; not today's Mars. Uranus has Uranus's 84-year year and Earth's light: that needs a bright, heavy star (about 7 Suns) far away; such a star lives only some 50 million years, the game bends that.
